newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd sees shipping rates under pressure in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd sees shipping rates under pressure in Q4.

text.p: Transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV said it expected shipping rates to stay under pressure in the fourth 1996 quarter.
"We anticipate that, in the Ocean Shipping sector, the pressure on rates will continue during the fourth quarter," it said in a statement accompanying its third quarter results.
Other main points from Nedlloyd's statement were:
* Operating profit fell to 17 million guilders from 32 million.
* But after stripping out capital gains on assets sold, operating profit showed an improvement of 27 million guilders.
* Positive volume effects, cost reductions and favourable movements in European currency rates compensated a drop in shipping rates versus Q3 1995 which cost 80 million guilders.
* Operating profit was unchanged from third quarter of 1995 at 23 million guilders.
* Groupage activities of Nedlloyd Unitrans in Germany continued to improve as expected.
* Result of Van Gend & Loos in Netherlands was lower, due in particular to start-up costs of new terminal in Eindhoven where three separate companies were integrated.
* Contribution from minority participations fell to 24 million guilders from 35 million.
* Charter airline Martinair's result deteriorated due to higher fuel costs and persistent pressure on air fares. NET INTEREST CHARGES
* Proceeds of Neddrill sale were used to reduce interest-bearing debt. Consequently net interest charges fell to 23 million guilders from 32 million.
